title: Corinthians Faces Fluminense: Protest and Penalty Define Encounter
seoTitle: Corinthians vs Fluminense: Protest, Penalty Mark Match
subtitle: What motivated the fans to turn their backs and Memphis's reaction
excerpt: Corinthians returns to the pitch against Fluminense at Neo Química Arena, following a Gaviões da Fiel protest and a Libertadores penalty miss that disappointed fans.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
At Neo Química Arena, Corinthians will face Fluminense this Sunday in a match that could seal Fernando Diniz's continuity as coach. The game follows a protest by Gaviões da Fiel, the main organized fan group, who turned their backs to the field before kickoff, after the National Anthem, and Memphis Depay's assumed blame for a missed penalty in the Libertadores.

Protest at Neo Química Arena

Members of Gaviões da Fiel turned their backs to the field before Monday's match against Fluminense, in the 28th round of the Brazilian Championship. The protest took place after the National Anthem and included chants like "it's not easy, you have to be a man to play for Coringão" and "let's play ball, oh, oh, oh" in the stands of Itaquera. Fans turned back to face the field when the referee blew the whistle for the start of the game.

Memphis Depay Apologizes

The forward took responsibility for the penalty missed in the match against Estudiantes, which eliminated Corinthians from the Libertadores. In a lengthy statement, Memphis described the penalty as the biggest disappointment of his career and apologized to the fans. He emphasized that the error was fatal and that the Libertadores dream was now in the past. The statement also mentions that Corinthians now only has the Brasileirão to compete in.

Impact on Diniz's Tenure

Corinthians has not won in five rounds of the Brasileirão and was eliminated from the Libertadores last Wednesday. The result against Fluminense could be decisive for Fernando Diniz's continuity. Leaders of the main organized fan groups have already visited CT Joaquim Grava to speak with part of the squad and demand explanations about the team's attitude in recent matches.

What to Expect from the Clash

The game is scheduled for 4 PM (Brasília time) and could be crucial for Timão's journey in the championship. The fans are in a climate of anticipation, while the squad tries to recover from a negative streak and a moment of economic crisis that has been cited as a pressure factor.

Conclusion

With the fans' protest and Memphis's blame, Corinthians takes to the field under pressure to prove its ability to overcome challenges and reverse its situation in the Brasileirão.
